READABILITY.evidence: Names reveal intent: buildWindowClause, validateWindowName, WindowDefinition, windowSql. The dialect changes follow the existing havingSql/orderBySql style, and the frame/arg validation tests read clearly. No cryptic names are visible in the diff.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One shared buildWindowClause is used in all five dialects, which is good. But each .window() repeats the same ~20-line callback/SelectionProxyHandler block five times, not the thin method the conventions asked for. buildWindowClause is also exported through '~/sql/index.ts'.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Inputs are validated where they enter: ntile/nthValue reject 0, negatives, fractions and NaN; preceding/following reject NaN and Infinity; from>to is rejected, including equal unbounded bounds; empty and whitespace window names are rejected. All 130/130 hidden tests pass.

C6-02-CASE1.evidence: Changes are additive only. Each of the five *SelectConfig types gets an optional 'windows?: WindowDefinition[]', and pg/mysql/sqlite/gel/singlestore all get the same .window(). windowSql is undefined when no window is set, so existing SQL is unchanged (P2P 566/566).
